## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ṭhita-sikkhāpada* ("Standing", Sekhiya 70) is a training rule for Buddhist monks preserved in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule belongs to the *sekhiya* class of regulations concerning proper etiquette and decorum, specifically in the context of teaching the Dhamma. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule possesses extensive parallels across early Buddhist monastic traditions. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to the monastic code proper (*Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* Sekhiya 70), the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and the parallel regulations for nuns in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. Outside the Theravāda transmission, corresponding rules are found in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions.
